merged.title: fix(editor): read the levels below normal priority, leaving threads free
merged.author: BlindFire1200
merged.untrustedBody:
## fix(editor): read the levels below normal priority, leaving threads free

### What this fixes

`editor/extract.py port` runs the launcher's **Get the levels ready** step (part of "Get levels and play"). It started one process per CPU thread at normal priority, so reading the levels took every thread and could leave the computer unresponsive until it finished. The build (`tools/build_port.py`) and the lighting bake (`bake_all.py`) already avoid this through `openrac_common.background`; the extract now does the same.

### Changes

- The `port` and `godot` exports call `background.lower_priority()` before starting work, and the level processes inherit the lower priority.
- `--jobs` now defaults to `background.cpu_budget()`: every thread except an eighth of them, keeping at least two free.
- `OPENRAC_EXTRACT_JOBS` overrides the default with a number or `all`, the same way `OPENRAC_BUILD_JOBS` works for the build. The launcher's step inherits the variable, so it can be set without a laun

merged.title: fix(port): mask failing 2D pixels on a multisampled frame instead of discarding them
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody: With anti-aliasing on, the menu text vanished on Intel Arc while the panels stayed. The text is the 2D path's only alpha-tested draw there, and its failing pixels used discard. On a multisampled frame those pixels now clear their sample mask instead, which writes the same nothing; a single-sample target still discards.

merged.title: feat(frontend): smoother frame limiter (precise waits, front edge sync)
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the frame cap and the game's tick waited with a plain sleep, which wakes late by its own amount (about 0.1 ms on Linux, 1 ms or more on Windows). A capped frame was held by its start, so the time it reached the screen moved with its cost. With VSync off, frame times were uneven, around 1–2 ms of spread at 120–240 fps.

**After:** every wait (tick, cap, low-latency sleep, movies) ends within a few microseconds of its deadline. With VSync off, a cap above the tick rate and Low-latency frames off, frames are held to the moment they are shown, as RTSS's front edge sync does. Simulated spread at 144 fps drops from 2.0 to 0.27 ms. VSync on, Low-latency frames, caps of 60 or less and mailbox/Android presents keep the old pacing, now with the precise wait.

**How:**
- `common/precise_wait`: the system sleeps to a learned margin before the deadline (a high-resolution waitable timer on Windows, `clock_nanosleep` with `TIMER_ABSTIME` on Linux/Android), then spins with the CPU pause hi

merged.title: fix(rac1): a landing with a full moby pool skips its missing actors
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody: The ship's landing (FlightUpdate) moves every actor of its scene each frame without checking for 0. When the moby pool was full the scene actor guard left an actor's slot empty, and the landing read through the null moby: Blarg Station crashed with the difficulty mod's extra enemies. While the update runs, the missing actors are now left out of its list and put back after it.

merged.title: Expand RAC1 modded level authoring and runtime limits
merged.author: ReaperOfVeriod
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

This PR contains the full local work since the modded-map editor effort began (93 commits across editor, launcher, and RAC1 runtime):

- Permit larger modded RAC1 gameplay/core streams with virtual sectors and a mod-only expanded guest-memory path, while ordinary vanilla sessions retain the original 32 MiB arena.
- Extend RAC1 moby and collision capacities and guard allocation/overflow paths used by larger maps.
- Improve Godot map authoring for collision edits, static GLB/glTF scenery, animated scenery, typed camera pvars, added cameras, and rebuilt camera-volume grids.
- Improve launcher guidance and pack validation for expanded maps and scenery.

The game disc image is never modified; the expanded path is selected for modded virtual streams.

## Validation

- Camera/gameplay-data tests: 33 pass.
- Full editor suite: 417 tests, with four existing failures (two moby class-change expectations and two Game-transform fixtures) and three skipped.
- `git diff --check` passes.

merged.title: fix(port): gamepads behind a USB-C dock and switching controllers
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** port 0 was the first gamepad SDL found. A USB-C dock or hub can add a device that SDL also lists as a gamepad (Android counts anything with a d-pad), so it took port 0. A controller plugged into the dock, or a Bluetooth one used with it, did nothing. Picking up a second controller mid-game did nothing either, since it stayed on port 1.

**After:** gamepads take ports in the order they are first pressed; ones never pressed come last. A gamepad pressed while port 0's has been idle for 2 s (no press, no stick moved, nothing held) takes port 0. Two players playing at once keep their ports.

**How:** `platform/input.cpp` keeps the gamepads in port order with each one's last activity time. Checks run only on a button press. An unplugged gamepad also clears its stick shape, so a new one opened at the same address starts fresh. The connect log now shows vendor:product.

**Tested:** new `input_ports` test with SDL virtual gamepads (dock first, two players, hand-over, held button/sti

merged.title: fix(hostgen): PAL freeze after picking Quartu
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** on PAL, flying from Kalebo to Quartu faded to a dim still picture and stayed there. The game had already autosaved, so after a restart you were on Quartu.

**After:** the flight loads Quartu.

**How:** PAL calls `scale_game_frame_count` through a cast, `((s32 (*)(s32))func_001F98C0)(12)`. hostgen sent that call through `OPENRAC_CODE`. No level copy was found, so the address stayed 0x1F98C0, and level 16's own function at that address ran instead. Its result made the fade wait about 1.4M frames. A cast call to a plain executable function is now a direct call, the same as a call by name. In PAL this changes 14 call sites. 13 of them sit below the relocated range, so they call the same function as before.

The second commit logs which wait a game is stuck in when no picture comes.

**Tested:** I ran the tester's presses on the PAL disc (Kalebo ship, select Quartu). The old build stays on level 16, and the new one reaches level 15. hostgen tests pass, and ctest passes 206 of 20

merged.title: fix(launcher): fade in a tab's list on WebKitGTK as on Chromium
merged.author: bigbeno37
merged.untrustedBody:
## Problem

On Linux, going from Settings to Mods, the list on the left pops in at the end of the slide. In Chromium, the engine behind WebView2 on Windows, it fades in.

## Fix

- **Fade (`SideFrame.svelte`):** WebKitGTK stops drawing the sticky list if `<main>` becomes scrollable mid-slide. The list and the page now scroll in their own columns, so `<main>` never scrolls on these tabs.
- **First press (`motion.ts`, `App.svelte`):** opening Mods in the first 2 seconds also left the list out of the slide, on both engines. `slide()` now waits for a lazily loaded page's code, for 1 second at most.

Behaviour change: a mouse wheel over the list no longer scrolls the page.

## Videos

Settings, Games, Settings, Mods. Watch the list when Mods opens.

**Before**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c8a634a-945a-4cb5-ba0d-2512d6826980

**After**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7ed8fb5-446f-4858-b3eb-d17f48815633

## Verified

- `yarn verify`: 221 t

merged.title: feat(enhanced): native baking, compressed probes and water materials
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
This is very WIP enhanced-rendering work. It moves automatic preparation into `openrac-enhanced-baker`, adds compressed GPU-ready probe colour, and improves water, wet character materials and fur while reducing redundant renderer work.

- Run water, emission, interior inference, GI and reflection baking in one native pipeline with shared worker and memory budgets, recoverable publication and profile-driven inputs.
- Encode BC6H on compatible desktop GPUs or ASTC HDR 8x8 on compatible hardware, retaining uncompressed visibility/metadata and supported format fallbacks. Use 256-ray MIS transport and parallel encoding.
- Add water transmission, shoreline blending, bicubic heights, lily controls, projectile/explosion interactions, wet reflections and directional Ratchet fur. Group the enhanced controls by feature.
- Reuse visibility, shadow preparation, buffer/history storage and draw setup; retain reference paths. Volumetric transport remains optional and off by default.
- Preserve u

merged.title: fix(port): plain 2D fills reach the screen's right and bottom edge
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** on the captions on black before a story movie (e.g. Veldin to Novalis), a thin line of the old level showed along the right and bottom edge.

**After:** the screen is black up to its edges.

**How:** the game draws its fills and fades from -0.5 to 511.5. The PS2 fills every pixel whose sample is inside, so the whole screen. The port drew them at those positions and left the last half pixel unfilled. A plain (untextured) sprite that covers the screen's last column or line now goes on to the screen's edge; edges inside the screen do not move. No game logic changes.

**Tested:** new renderer_gif_test case; ctest 212/213 pass (xcheck_tool fails without this change too); Veldin to Novalis captions in the container: right column and bottom row were bright before, black after, every other pixel the same (also the pause menu). Not run: render_equivalence (too slow on software GL), real device.

merged.title: fix(port): planet name in the flight between planets, and a shorter stop after it
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
- A flight started from a planet hid the destination's name: the planet's level program is still loaded then, the flight's 2D was split as a level's frame and drawn before the world, and the stars covered the name.
- While the game sent no picture after the flight (waiting on the load), the window drew the last flight frame again with textures the load had replaced: the name as a solid block, the planet striped.
- After the flight the port read the next level's files (models, textures, placements) before drawing it: about 1.6 s with the game stopped on an Odin 3, and the sound ran ahead.

## After
- The name fades in as on the console, wherever the flight starts.
- The last picture stands while the game sends none.
- The next level's files are read on another thread during the flight; the level change only uploads them.

## How
- `capture_2d_path`: no world split when the world drawn is the flight's (`world_to_draw` < 0).
- `keep_picture`: repeats the last frame instead of dr

merged.title: fix(rac1): check collision.c against the retail kernels; no gl_SampleMask without MSAA
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
Before
- collision.c (host C of the collision kernels) could not be checked against the game's own code, and differed from it in small ways.
- With anti-aliasing off, Adreno drew a flickering checkerboard over menu panels (the Quit Game box on Oltanis). Since #145 the 2D shader wrote gl_SampleMask on every target.

After
- hostgen can translate chosen asm functions a second time as "shadows" with PS2 float arithmetic. OPENRAC_COLL_CHECK=1 runs every collision query through both and logs any difference (docs/port/DEBUGGING.md).
- Fixed in collision.c: hit and vf2 use the real VU0 registers, line queries take vf2.w from the face and primitive loads, hit normals and primitive points store -0 as +0, sphere-mobys and hero-groups start vf2.w at 0.
- gl_SampleMask is only in a second 2D program used on a multisampled frame; everywhere else a failing pixel is discarded as before #145.

Tested
- OPENRAC_COLL_CHECK on levels 0-18 (NTSC): about 1M queries, 0 differences.
- regress befo

merged.title: fix(rac1): keep the console arena's 224 moby class slots
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody: #148 made the run-list builder clear and chain 256 class slots in every session; retail does 224. Use 256 only with expanded RAM, and drop the size-byte check it added to collision's retail cell path.

opened.title: chore(import): sync rac1 to rac1-decomp 693667f2 and Lombyte d2980748
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
Brings rac1/pal to rac1-decomp 693667f2 and rac1/ntsc to Lombyte d2980748 (#267 game data in C, #268 name batch 35, #269 moby updates named `<name>_update`).

- rac1/pal: the one doc-comment commit, applied cleanly.

opened.title: perf(port): speed up Vulkan regression tests
opened.author: pezzadev
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Vulkan regression checks spend too much time rebuilding identical scenes
and compiling unused shaders on software CI. Reuse fixed renderer setups
while keeping fresh determinism baselines, all 742 registry comparisons,
existing tolerances, level reuploads and poisoned-attachment checks.

- Share normal-fixture resources and separate receiver-normal checks into
  a focused source/header pair.
- Load only the lighting metadata needed by effect-material checks; run
  duplicate standalone shadow kernels once while retaining both production
  filter paths.
- Compile GTAO quality kernels on demand, with a quality-switch regression.
- Use faster Mesa compilation in enhanced Ubuntu CI. Keep normal LLVM
  optimisation for the arithmetic-heavy horizon reference and Fedora.

merged.title: tools: expand li.s as SN's assembler does; PAL C for 27 functions it unblocks
merged.author: chistianh
merged.untrustedBody:
**Title:** tools: expand li.s as SN's assembler does; PAL C for 27 functions it unblocks

### The tool change

GCC writes every float constant as `li.s $fN, value`. Retail's assembler, SN's `ps2eeas`, always builds the value in `$at`: `lui`, plus `ori` when the low half is not zero, then `mtc1`. The driver's GNU `as` does that only when the low half is zero. For any other value, at -G8, it puts the value in `.lit4` and loads it with one `lwc1 ...($gp)`. That is one word instead of three, plus a `$gp` access retail does not have. So no function with a float constant like 0.3 or 1.6 could match.

- I checked it on `ps2eeas` itself (`toolchain/sn-prodg-3.01/.../Ps2EeAs.exe`, 1.9.25) on test files: `li.s $f12, 0.08` becomes `lui $at, 0x3DA3; ori $at, $at, 0xD70B; mtc1 $at, $f12`.
- In the PAL text the `lui`/`ori`/`mtc1 $at` form appears 13,207 times.
- `tools/ps2eeas_lis.py` (new, in the SN route of `tools/cc.sh` after `ps2eeas_dli.py`) writes that sequence out before the first assembly. `

The submission, review, Discussions and broken-index jobs now act as openrac-bot (its name and logo, and its PRs start CI), each with a one-hour token scoped to that job; the default workflow token drops to read-only there.
Verified: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests passes, both workflows parse; actionlint and zizmor run in this PR's CI.
